end.summary:
Practised properties and classification of parallelograms, rhombuses, squares, kites and trapeziums.
Myra identified that a square has four equal sides and can also be a rhombus; the tilted-shape misconception was corrected later.
Myra continued to state that a parallelogram must have unequal adjacent sides; this was not corrected by the end.
Perimeter calculation given: 5 + 5 + 8 + 8 = 26 cm.
Myra reported being hit when a parent is angry and feeling afraid to go home; they said they were safe at school during the lesson.
end.parentNote: Asha practised sorting quadrilaterals by their properties and used side, angle, diagonal and perimeter information. Myra used the equal-side property to recognise a square as a rhombus after initially linking rhombuses only with a tilted appearance. The idea that a rhombus can also be a parallelogram still needs revisiting, along with kite and trapezium properties. Myra also disclosed fear of going home and being hit when a parent is angry; this needs prompt safeguarding attention through the appropriate school or child-protection process.
